ProblemSolution.heading: Palestinians Don't Need More Sympathy. They Need Economic Opportunity.

capital.title: Businesses have ideas but no access to capital
capital.body: Talented entrepreneurs have the skills, experience, and determination to build businesses, but cannot access the funding needed to start or grow.

trust.title: Millions want to help, but don't know how
trust.body: Palestinians in the diaspora and ethical supporters around the world want to contribute, yet there is no trusted and transparent way to invest in local businesses.

aid.title: Aid solves today's problem, not tomorrow's
aid.body: Traditional aid helps families survive, but when the money is spent, the impact often ends there.

jobs.title: Skilled people remain unemployed
jobs.body: Engineers, teachers, designers, craftsmen, and business owners are ready to work but lack opportunities to create income.

dependence.title: Communities depend on continuous assistance
dependence.body: Without sustainable businesses, communities remain dependent on external support rather than creating their own economic growth.

capital.title: Entrepreneurs receive the capital they need
capital.body: Qualified Palestinian business owners receive funding to launch, rebuild, or expand businesses with real growth potential.

trust.title: Supporters directly fund economic growth
trust.body: Every contribution becomes an investment in a real entrepreneur, a real business, and a real future.

aid.title: One contribution creates lasting impact
aid.body: Instead of supporting a family for a week, a funded business can create jobs and income for years.

jobs.title: Businesses create jobs for Palestinians
jobs.body: Every successful business becomes an economic engine that hires workers, serves customers, and strengthens the local economy.

dependence.title: Success funds the next entrepreneur
dependence.body: Profitable businesses contribute back to Bidhra, allowing future entrepreneurs to receive support and creating a self-sustaining cycle of growth.

Problems.heading: Aid keeps them alive. Investment gives them a life.
Problems.subheading: How long will we keep donating, while Palestinians wait to build?

collapse.title: The economy is broken
collapse.statCaption: How much smaller the Palestinian economy is since the war
collapse.body: Gaza needs $71 billion to rebuild. The West Bank can barely trade. 3.5 million Palestinians at home and 7 million abroad need a new way to earn. Not the one that's holding them back.

displacement.title: Pushed out, cut off
displacement.statCaption: Palestinians living outside Palestine, with no way to help home
displacement.body: War pushed Palestinians out of Palestine. Many are starting over in Egypt, Jordan, Turkey, Europe, and North America. Those who stayed have no easy way to receive help from those who left. People abroad want to help. People at home need it. Nothing connects them.

aid.title: Aid feeds. It does not build.
aid.statCaption: Share of people in Gaza now living on aid
aid.body: Aid keeps people alive, but it does not build anything. When the aid stops, nothing is left behind. One dollar of food aid is eaten once. One dollar in a small business is spent again and again, making $4 to $7 of new local activity.

unemployment.title: Skilled people, no work
unemployment.statCaption: Of people in Gaza have no job, and 32% in the West Bank
unemployment.body: Hundreds of thousands of skilled Palestinians sit at home with nothing to do. Engineers, teachers, designers, builders, farmers, shopkeepers. A whole generation is losing its skills and its hope. That talent is going to waste.

Manifesto.eyebrow: Why a business, not a meal
Manifesto.heading: Food runs out. A business doesn't.
Manifesto.lede: Most aid in Gaza keeps people alive. That matters. But survival isn't a future.
Manifesto.body: Bidhra funds the next step: the bakery that reopens, the seamstress who buys a new machine, the shop owner who restocks his shelves. When you give to Bidhra, you're not feeding one family for one week. You're restarting a business that will feed dozens of families for years.
Manifesto.closing: Every dollar you give goes directly into the hands of a Palestinian business owner who has a plan, a skill, and a will to rebuild.

examples.seamstress: A seamstress buys a new machine
examples.shop: A shop owner restocks his shelves

HowItWorks.heading: The seed grows into a tree. The tree drops new seeds.

apply.title: A Palestinian applies
apply.body: Any Palestinian, anywhere, applies with a business idea, or one that needs to grow. To be accepted, <promise>they make two promises:</promise> hire only Palestinians who need work, and share a part of future profits to fund the next business.

verify.title: Bidhra verifies
verify.body: Our team checks every applicant through video calls, references, and a clear plan. No anonymous projects. No middlemen. Every owner we approve is real, named, and answerable.

fund.title: Supporters fund the seed
fund.body: People in the diaspora and ethical supporters contribute $50, $500, or more. Every contribution is tracked. Every dollar is shown in public.

build.title: The business builds. The community grows.
build.body: The owner opens the business and hires Palestinians who need work. Supporters follow the journey through updates, photos, and videos. One funded business becomes a small employer.

forest.title: The seed becomes a forest
forest.body: When the business turns a profit, it gives back a share to Bidhra. That money funds the next Palestinian business. Then that one funds the next. And so on.

HowItWorks.closing: One funded family becomes a community. A community becomes an economy.

Footer.mission: Bidhra turns global support into sustainable economic opportunity for Palestinians — one verified business at a time.

CryptoExplainer.heading: Why crypto?
CryptoExplainer.body: Gaza's banking system has been severely disrupted by the conflict, making traditional wire transfers unreliable or impossible. USDT on the Tron network bypasses these barriers — funds reach Palestinian entrepreneurs directly, with low fees and within minutes.
CryptoExplainer.trc20Note: Lowest fees. Fastest settlement. Our recommended method.

HowToDonate.title: How to donate with USDT
HowToDonate.subtitle: A step-by-step guide for first-time crypto users. No experience needed.
HowToDonate.whyBody: Gaza's banks are largely inaccessible due to the conflict. USDT (a dollar-pegged cryptocurrency) on the Tron network bypasses those barriers — it's fast, cheap, and reaches Palestinian entrepreneurs directly.
HowToDonate.step1Body: Download a free crypto wallet app on your phone. We recommend Trust Wallet or Binance Web3 Wallet. Create an account and back up your 12-word seed phrase somewhere safe.
HowToDonate.step2Body: Inside your wallet app, use the built-in Buy feature to purchase USDT. Alternatively, use a crypto exchange like Binance, Coinbase, or Kraken — buy USDT, then withdraw it to your wallet address.
HowToDonate.step2Note: Make sure you select the Tron (TRC-20) network when buying or withdrawing. Sending on the wrong network means the funds don't arrive.
HowToDonate.step3Heading: Step 3 — Click 'Contribute money' on the project page
HowToDonate.step3Body: Choose your amount and fill in your details. After confirming, you'll be sent to a secure payment page provided by NOWPayments.
HowToDonate.step4Heading: Step 4 — Send USDT to the address shown
HowToDonate.step4Body: The NOWPayments page will show a wallet address and a QR code. In your wallet app, tap Send, paste the address (or scan the QR code), enter the exact USDT amount shown, and confirm the transaction.
HowToDonate.step4Note: Double-check the address before sending. Crypto transactions are irreversible.
HowToDonate.step5Body: Tron transactions typically confirm within 1–3 minutes. Once confirmed, your donation is recorded and the project's raised total updates automatically.
HowToDonate.faq1Q: Is USDT the same as US dollars?
HowToDonate.faq1A: Yes — USDT (Tether) is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the US dollar. $100 USDT equals $100 USD.
HowToDonate.faq2A: TRC-20 is a token standard on the Tron blockchain. It's the cheapest and fastest way to send USDT — fees are typically less than $1.
HowToDonate.faq3A: We only accept USDT on the Tron (TRC-20) network. Ethereum fees are much higher and we cannot guarantee receipt of other networks.
HowToDonate.faq4A: Yes — you'll receive a confirmation email once your payment is verified on-chain. Your donation will also appear on the campaign page.
